registry_rules: A non-grant authorization source is active only when one exact active row is selected by authority_source_id; syntax or an arbitrary Event reference never creates authority.

The current governance Station rederives activation, actor, resource and lifecycle predicates from its authority-committed current state and fails closed on missing, conflicting, non-canonical or freshness-unknown dependencies.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create carrying both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=principal_control create carrying only one of the two matches no variant and is denied with zero writes. For purpose=agent_control the immutable accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision is resolved by its whole-value claim of retype(this EventId, realm); the genesis MUST NOT carry a backward agent_provision ref, which would create an EventId cycle. The verifier cross-binds the complete actor/controller AccountIds, PCR delegation and provision payload before materializing Agent status. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch proves its separate accepted organization authority. A self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis: a purpose=principal_control ak.realm.create carrying neither executed_by nor authorization_ref. The create carries no DID-inception Event reference, because DID inception is method-native material and not an Arkret Event. Registration-time DID control evidence is the frozen typed principal_registration_anchor carried by the genesis submission: the verifier rebuilds the registration-time DID, terminal version / history head, normalized DID Document and then-active update key from that one anchor, recomputes SHA-256 over its RFC 8785 JCS bytes and requires the result to equal the identity creation control proof registration_anchor_digest. It validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant. The selector only routes to this verifier and proves no authorization: a create that reaches it without the complete ordered genesis unit, anchor and accepted receipt closure is still rejected with zero writes.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical semantic_refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the root-round responder; glare branch: the full signed request Event author ActorId referenced by requests[0], never the Station receipt issuer_id; requests MUST be strictly ascending by the complete request_event_ref wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes, with duplicate Event refs rejected regardless of receipt digest and no receiver-side sorting or deduplication), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked baseline: genesis initial_join_rule=closed, initial_discoverability=invite_only and initial_history_access=since_join are constants, and any other value rejects the whole unit with direct_conversation_founding_unit_invalid. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.sidecar_account_self_authored_proof: Admitted only when Event actor_id is the account branch and its complete AccountId is the authenticated controller account. The reducer derives controller_account_id byte-for-byte from actor_id.account_id, uses (realm_id, controller_account_id) as the singleton key, and rejects the service actor branch with sidecar_create_denied before revealing existence. The same exact AccountId binds Sidecar membership, MLS genesis and participant authority; principal-only equality is forbidden.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.agent_controller_self_authored_proof: Only a current active controller account may sign a Realm-scoped ak.agent.interaction.set for its exact active member Agent. Author, authenticated account and payload controller AccountId must match in both components; current provision/accountability, controller membership generation, device authorization and expected_revision CAS are checked before any effects. Service authors, Agent self-writes, administrators and executed_by delegation cannot substitute. No capability grants authority for this class. See models/agent-interaction.md section 1.
admission_class_definitions.capability_or_owned_agent: Ordinary capability admission remains required except for ak.capability.grant with the sole closed owned_agent source, or ak.capability.revoke of that source by its original issuer/controller. The source grants only explicitly registered terminal actions; exact account ownership/membership, current controller ceiling, global/key bounds and Agent policy are mandatory. Revoke needs no action authority, active join or runtime, but requires original issuer proof, signing eligibility and exact target CAS. Administrators and other targets use ordinary capability admission. See zh/authz/owned-agent-authority.md.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field to be present, and top_level_fields_absent requires every listed field to be absent, evaluated member by member. A member that is present with a null value still counts as present and is still subject to that member's own schema, so top_level_fields_absent is not a 'not both present' selector; the two field selectors MUST NOT appear in one when object. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.semantic_refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry and resolve to exactly one closed payload schema.
An accepted durable Event becomes shared history only when the current authority includes its exact bytes in a signed RealmCommit for the Event's own Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream.
Stream identity is derived from the Event's closed scope. Realm, each Circle, and each Sidecar have independent commit streams; no Realm-global total chain exists.
Event carries no chain predecessor or authority-commit proof. Only RealmCommit carries previous_commit_ref, and only within the same stream.
Reducers derive typed current results by replaying committed Events in stream position order. Account-private material is outside shared authority-commit streams.

wire_scope=durable_event does NOT imply reducer_input=true. A durable Event is one whose exact bytes a RealmCommit can cover; reducer_input=true additionally asserts that replaying this Realm's committed Events suffices to derive the typed current results the kind writes. A kind whose real durable effect is holder-Station private service state -- keyed on material that never enters the Event stream, or on a counterpart mirror that zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 3 forbids from advancing a reducer -- MUST carry reducer_input=false and MUST name the canonical service_contracts row that spells out its branches, durable effect, unique key, prior-state CAS, exact retry and zero-side-effect rejection. Withdrawing Realm typed-result dispatch never withdraws the kind's admission, signature, commit evidence or private transactional effect: the five ak.contact.* kinds are the worked example (ak.contact.admission.v1). Setting reducer_input=false without registering where the effect actually lands is the defect this rule exists to prevent.

result_writes[] is the machine contract for which typed current results one Event kind writes, in what order, and under which closed condition; zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10 read it as the source of truth, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_contracts validates every declared row: a declared value_projection member MUST be declared by that row's value_schema_ref, and a whole-value set MUST write every member that schema requires. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THIS IS A KNOWN GAP: 118 of the 122 reducer_input kinds declare it; the remaining 4 have an explicit durable-fact or authority-commit effect classification and intentionally no typed-current-result row. The declaring kinds are deliberately not enumerated here: event_kinds[] already is that list, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_coverage_note recomputes both counts from the rows. Normative prose MUST NOT cite result_writes[] for a kind that does not declare it. The converse obligation binds a declaring kind: its rows MUST enumerate EVERY typed current result its accepted admission writes on the shared face; atomic multi-family writes land all rows in one batch or none.

Every active persistent kind (durable_event or actor_private_event) MUST carry one closed result_effect_ownership object. A typed_result_writer owns non-empty result_writes[] and no second owner; a private_service_effect names an active service_contracts row whose branches cover that exact actor-private Event kind; a durable_fact_no_current_projection names its normative definition and carries no typed-current-result write; an authority_commit_effect names the structured authority-commit service contract and MUST NOT introduce a second governance counter; an owned_gap is temporary only while it names a live owner_report and exact closure condition. Unknown classifications, unresolved definitions, orphan service branches, shared/private mixing, malformed authority contracts or any classification that contradicts reducer_input/result_writes[] fail tools/artifact_lint:result_effect_ownership.

transition_contracts declares the lifecycle axis of a typed current result family: its closed state set, its entry idiom (exactly one of initial_state / initial_states / template), its terminal states and its allowed (from, to) edges. tools/artifact_lint:fsm_reachability reads it together with every transition result_projection and requires that each declared state be reachable from the entry set, that each allowed edge have a write that can perform it, that no const edge leave the table and that no terminal state carry an outgoing edge. A family that declares a machine MUST NOT be written by any non-transition projection: a set installs a state without passing the table, which would make allowed_transitions documentation rather than a rule. Between the authority-commit clean break and 2026-09-18 this block did not exist while the gate still read it under the removed cell_* names, so check reported success over four normative paragraphs (zh/models/circle.md, zh/models/morph.md, zh/models/realm-and-space.md, zh/models/strand-and-message.md) that name transition_contracts as the source of truth for object lifecycle transitions; an absent or empty block is now a failure. Those four object families are themselves still unregistered, so their archive / restore lifecycle has no machine contract yet -- that is a coverage gap, not a licence to read the prose as satisfied.

Dot-bearing keyed sets serialize by the tuple (complete event_id in unsigned UTF-8 byte order, numeric write_index). write_index is canonical decimal without leading zeros. Duplicate dots or one dot with conflicting values are rejected, never silently folded. This ordering is not authority or causal ordering.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Only x_* fields explicitly admitted by a concrete payload schema are non-critical extensions; they are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Current-v1 has no generic Event requirements or critical_extensions carrier. New critical semantics require a new or upgraded registered kind/schema and a complete activation package.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

event_kinds.payload: Actor-private account data update. The closed signed payload carries the integer expected_server_revision for server_revision_cas; expected_revision is the distinct shared-result revision type and is not an alias.

Controller-signed one-shot publication authorization in the target Realm safety sequence. approved_event_id binds the complete pre-authored Event. The same confirmed command allocates (controller ActorId, approval_nonce) once; it is not a reusable private approval followed by receiver-local consumption. The original Event remains ordinary data and requires this exact confirmation only when its explicit approval constraint applies.

result_writes.notes: authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.6. approval_id selects the immutable confirmation record. Before this write the reducer verifies controller authority, exact agent/draft/request and approved_event_id binding, covering RealmCommit committed_at <= payload.expires_at (inclusive, zero tolerance; envelope created_at and Station-local time are never compared; a late confirmation fails with generic failed_precondition without a dedicated reason and allocates no nonce), and uniqueness of (envelope.actor_id, payload.approval_nonce). The approved Event's own publication gate applies the same inclusive comparison to its covering committed_at; a late Event is treated as lacking a valid confirmation and fails with claim_required reason approval_required and zero writes. Exact replay returns the original Commit and outcome without re-judging expiry; nonce reuse for different bytes fails with approval_nonce_reused and writes nothing.

event_kinds.payload: Controller rejection of one actor-private action request, named by request_id. The request transitions to rejected; the agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts for it. Drafts are not rejection targets: their workflow_state is controller-encrypted Account Data.

Agent-initiated action request. Carries proposed_action, target descriptor and request_canonical_digest, the digest of the complete pre-authored Event awaiting controller approval before it is submitted.

Agent-initiated draft proposal. Acceptance creates one structured Station-private pending intent with HPKE content handoff after capability / policy / accountability / risk checks. A controller holder device later creates encrypted ak.agent.draft.v1 account data through the unique account-data CAS. Station MUST NOT generate ciphertext, hold the holder secret, treat the pending intent as account data, or enter it into shared Realm history.

Controller-only per-Realm interaction mode with exact expected_revision CAS; plaintext control, never a membership, Account Data or private participation write. Circle and Strand inherit the Realm mode and only narrow ordinary permissions. Verified never-written defaults to private; unknown fails closed. Mode transitions do not change membership or Sidecar MLS participants. models/agent-interaction.md sections 1-5.

result_writes.notes: models/agent-interaction.md section 1. Realm is the source stream, not a subject component. Same-value writes still advance revision. CAS, exact current ownership and controller-only signing are atomic guards. expected_revision is never stored; no MLS or member writes occur. Current mode is independently checked at every shared Agent action admission.

event_kinds.payload: Agent key authorization is a commit-ordered projection security command with complete explicit revocation set representation. Same-key replacement removes all authorization dots visible at the signed basis and adds one replacement dot, after exact revision and authority checks at execution. Competing replacements cannot survive as concurrent permission heads. Runtime replacement pairs a new raw key and revokes prior active keys in the same confirmed transaction.

result_writes.notes: identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1 fixes the order: the reducer MUST first project, for every payload.supersedes[] item, a remove of the observed canonical Event dot named by that item's authorized_event_ref on the OLD key subject, and only then add the new authorization. So this is write_index 0 and the add below is write_index 1. The subject moves per item, which is why the selector reads item.key_id while the add reads payload.key_id; payload.supersedes is the exact complete active authorization set at expected_revision, bounded at 256 items, so the loop is closed rather than open. Removing the exact observed dot rather than the whole observed set is what makes same-key re-authorization and replacement supersede provable from the signed RealmCommit without a service-private key table.

identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1: the stable element tag is the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot of models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 and never a bare event_id, and the element value is the complete authorize payload. The current-row locator MUST come from the registered family-specific derive_agent_key_current_key(agent_id, key_id) typed API and MUST NOT be spelled by a generic composite helper, string concatenation or a diagnostic subject; agent_key_result.selector carries the two components separately for the same reason. ak.agent.key.revoke is the family's second normative writer and is now registered. Its removal is scoped to the active authorize dots alone, spelled as the existence predicate {element_field: verification_method, present: true}: agent_key_authorization_entry.value is a oneOf of agent_key_authorize_payload and agent_key_revoke_payload, both additionalProperties:false with disjoint required sets, so verification_method is present on every authorize element and forbidden on every revocation marker.

event_kinds.payload: Agent signing-key revocation. The current governance Station verifies the controller and active key, then commits the exact Event on its authority stream; the payload carries no RealmCommit or authorization basis.

result_writes.notes: identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1 fixes the order -- remove the observed active authorize dots first, then add the boundary marker -- so this is write_index 0 and the add below is write_index 1. The removal is scoped to every ACTIVE AUTHORIZE dot and NOT to every observed element: the same sentence says a marker is not an active authorization, and line 163 of that file says an active set may be empty because a revoke came first and a re-attach followed, so an earlier marker is still in the observed set and MUST survive. A match-less removal takes every observed element in scope (zh/models/pins.md section 4.1) and would drop it. The filter is the existence predicate {element_field, present: true} on verification_method, which is required on agent_key_authorize_payload and forbidden on agent_key_revoke_payload -- both are additionalProperties:false with disjoint required sets, so agent_key_authorization_entry.value discriminates exactly. The equality spelling {element_field, source} cannot stand in, because no member of the revoke payload equals an authorize-only element member, and keyed_set_remove_dots needs a for_each array this payload does not carry. The marker's polarity is deliberately not an element field: models/common-fields.md section 2 makes reading it from the signed envelope normative for every keyed-set family.

identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1: the revocation boundary marker. The stable element tag is the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot of models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 and never a bare event_id -- this Event carries two writes on one subject, so a bare event_id would not even be unique within it. The element value is the complete revoke payload, unassembled. The marker records a witnessed revocation boundary and is NOT an active authorization; a reader tells it apart by the absence of verification_method, which is exactly the predicate write 0 removes by. The write 0 removal cannot reach this element: keyed_set_remove_observed only removes elements alive in the frozen prior state, and this one is added by the same Event.

admission_checks: payload.created_at equals envelope.created_at byte-for-byte; the accountability projection derives not_before from the envelope, so two signed times must not disagree

payload.accountability_scope normalizes to the same string set the typed current result subject digests, so this projection and a later ak.identity.accountability_grant address one typed current result

payload.controller_principal_id equals the principal component of envelope.actor_id; the create-locked ArkretPrincipalControlRealm serviceEndpoint compares its controller_did against the member this payload carries, so an unbound member would let one controller create-lock an Agent to another controller's DID
event_kinds.payload: Controller-authored Agent provisioning fact. One Event proof binds the allocated Agent DID, the forward-declared Agent PCR realm id, controller delegation, immutable requested-scope digest, accountability scope and selector. Admission atomically projects the agent_provisioning, identity_accountability, agent_selector_claim and agent_pcr_genesis_declaration typed results; no nested payload proof or partial two-Event state is valid. The declared Agent PCR genesis arrives in a later separate submission whose admission reverse-looks-up the realm-id declaration.

result_writes.notes: One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. The provisioning fact itself, keyed by the Agent DID alone. It is deliberately NOT keyed by the Agent's full account ActorId: models/actor.md derives that ActorId from payload.agent_id plus this Event's exact controller account and Station and only reconciles it against genesis.actor_id after genesis, and this Event's own envelope actor_id is the CONTROLLER, so an ActorId subject would be unconstructible here. The line in identity/key-management.md section 3.6 that forbids a bare DidCoreId subject governs the LIFECYCLE family, whose reason -- one principal on two Stations is two accounts -- is discharged in this family by the Realm component plus the same-Station rule of section 3.6.3. Every member is a plain signed-payload copy; requested_scope itself stays controller-private and only its digest is projected. A second provision declaring an agent_id an accepted provision already carries MUST be rejected with zero writes (agent_provisioning_already_declared) -- that rejection is admission semantics, not pre_state_requirements[], because every registered predicate is positive over a stored field and "no row for this subject" has no spelling.

One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. The second registered writer of the record ak.identity.accountability_grant also writes; models/actor.md section 3.3.1 fixes both to one subject and one canonical business value, and a later generic grant that changes this endorsement MUST be written into this same controller PCR. The scope component is digested and the stored member goes through normalized_string_set for the same reason the standalone writer does it: this payload's const is a bare string and the standalone payload MAY carry a one-element array, and both have to reach the same subject and the same stored value. not_before is envelope.created_at, which is safe to read here only because an admission check requires payload.created_at to equal it byte-for-byte -- two signed times MUST NOT disagree. grant_status is the literal active. expires_at is NOT projected: section 3.3.1 makes absence mean non-expiring and forbids both a JSON null and the server's receive time. source_event_ref and the inner proof are likewise absent -- the head Event and its acceptance proof carry provenance, and copying an event_id into the value would make two semantically identical endorsements unequal.

One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. This is the only registered writer of the family; there is no standalone selector-claim Event kind: models/actor.md section 3.3 keeps the principal-scoped subject (controller principal, agent_slug) with no Station component, and a later provision of the same slug replaces the binding. There is no inner selector proof and no portable signed-claim surface; a service MUST NOT mint one. subject_account_id comes from the registered derivation agent_account_id_from_provision -- principal from the signed payload.agent_id, station from this Event's own envelope.actor_id -- because select picks one field path and nothing in this grammar joins a payload principal to an envelope station; the value is still fully determinate on the wire. audience is projected only when the payload carries selector_audience, which its own schema makes conditional on selector_visibility being restricted. A provision selector binding does not expire on a clock. Until the Agent PCR genesis is accepted the Agent MUST NOT be treated as an active resolvable target, which is a resolution-side gate and not a reason to withhold this write.

One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. The forward declaration of an Agent PCR that does not exist yet -- the named class C preimage exemption of conformance/encoding.md §3.1. The subject is the declared realm id and the value is the one-member index naming the Agent, because both readers start from a realm id and nothing else: genesis admission holds retype(create.event_id) and DID entry 1 admission holds serviceEndpoint.realm_id. They resolve the Agent here and then read the remaining create-locked members from agent_provisioning keyed by it, so no member of the create-locked four-tuple lives in two families. A second provision declaring a realm id an accepted provision already claims MUST be rejected with zero writes (agent_pcr_genesis_declaration_conflict); this family covers one controller PCR and the Station's local uniqueness index covers the rest. The genesis carries no ref back to its provision, so a missing row MUST fail closed with agent_pcr_genesis_declaration_missing and materialize neither the Realm nor the agent_status transition.

branches.rejection: No contact round and no lineage is created; a terminated slot is never revived, and a mismatched request or receipt is rejected with zero side effects.

branches.durable_effect: Establish the normal contact round, this issuer directional initial state, and store the verified counterpart founding evidence.

branches.durable_effect: After verifying both requests and both receipts, durably store the single founding evidence and version 1 for each side direction.

branches.durable_effect: Replace the stored verification material (lease, checkpoint, current proof) for a direction.

branches.rejection: MUST NOT advance the business version and MUST NOT create a direction that does not exist.

registry_rules: A schema row with omitted status defaults to active. New or edited rows MUST spell status explicitly.
The only allowed schema status is active. Unknown or any non-active status fails closed; the registry defines no historical compatibility rows.

consumer_binding, when present, is the machine-readable disposition for a logical schema that is not directly named by an operation, Event kind, or another schema. Runtime and dynamic wire bindings MUST declare kind, selector, and normative_ref. A prose_only binding MUST instead declare a non-empty rationale and MUST NOT be counted as wire coverage.

The effective schema reference of a row is the literal concatenation (file + optional fragment): fragment already includes its leading '#', so consumers MUST NOT insert another separator. For example file='schemas/agent-operations.schema.json' plus fragment='#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap' resolves to exactly 'schemas/agent-operations.schema.json#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap'. Consumers MUST resolve that URI-fragment JSON Pointer and MUST NOT bind schema_id to the top-level document of file. When fragment is absent, the effective reference is the top-level document of file. Two schema_id rows mapping to the same file MUST be distinguished by fragment (or one MUST omit fragment to denote the whole document); a consumer that ignores fragment and loads the top-level document for a fragment-bearing row is non-conforming.

fragment, when present, MUST be a non-empty RFC 6901 JSON Pointer in URI-fragment representation starting with '#/'. If the pointer does not resolve within file, or a row that shares a file with another row omits fragment while that other row also omits fragment (ambiguous whole-document mapping), consumers MUST fail closed rather than silently pick a schema.

This registry lists WIRE schemas: objects that are signed, transmitted, or referenced by id through payload.schema or a DTO $ref. The VALUE shape of a typed current result is out of scope and MUST NOT get an ak.schema.* id of its own: it is a reducer output whose only registered read path is the value_schema_ref JSON Pointer on that family's result_writes[] rows, and an id would make one value look like a wire schema and invite binding by id instead of by the write contract. A whole-document id over typed-current-result.schema.json is fine -- ak.schema.result_projection.v1 is exactly that -- but a row whose fragment points at one value $defs member is not registrable, and the lint rejects one. The realm_authority_root_value row was the sole such row and was withdrawn; its writers always referenced the pointer, so nothing but the id was lost. See zh/sync/current-results.md section 1 and zh/conformance/schema-registry.md section 1.1.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

Every special_forms row declares payload_pattern, the machine-readable value space of everything after its ak:<kind>: prefix; wire_form remains the human-readable template and payload_pattern is its only normative expansion. A schema, OpenAPI or profile carrier MAY be narrower than payload_pattern for a specific field, but MUST NOT accept an octet payload_pattern rejects, and MUST end-anchor so no trailing byte escapes the declared value space.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

closed_encoding.audience_id: canonical_bare_resource_service_did; never an HTTP origin or endpoint URL
closed_encoding.credential_binding: credential_class is standard or recovery_session; holder_binding is required; device_binding is required only for standard human_device and forbidden for recovery_candidate_device and agent_runtime

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including credential_class and holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so different credential classes or holder bindings cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; standard human holder_binding and its complete device_binding carry accepted-device authority. Recovery candidate-device and Agent runtime holder bindings carry their own device_id and forbid device_binding.

lifecycle.refresh: one issuer transaction creates active successor and supersedes predecessor with successor_session_grant_id

account_status_record_identity_contract.digest_input: SHA-256(JCS(record fields excluding account_status_record_id and proof))
account_status_record_identity_contract.sequence_rule: status_seq starts at 1; seq=1 is active and has no previous_account_status_record_id; every successor is current+1 and names the exact current account_status_record_id

realm_token_layout.event_derived_retype_identity: Realm and Event token headers are identical, so an ak.realm.create Event token is byte-identical to its Realm token and retyping only swaps the ak:event: / ak:realm: prefix. v1 Realm identity is fixed to SHA-256, so only a creating Event with header 0x01 is Realm-eligible.
realm_token_layout.high_nibble_carries_no_category: The high nibble is reserved zero and carries no category information. Realm purpose lives in the signed create payload; implementations MUST NOT infer purpose from realm_id.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3); distinct from ak:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs. The embedded digest is the sole wire carrier of the referenced bytes' digest; same-carrier sibling digest mirrors are forbidden (encoding.md 4.0.1).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical value for equality and indexing; generic consumers MUST NOT split or normalize the adapter-defined core segment.
special_forms.description: Stable DID-derived principal, actor or service identity core. It is not a DID, is not directly resolvable, and MUST be projected only by a registered DID method adapter from a canonical bare did. Registered as a special form rather than an id_form because its identity authority is the external DID method, not an Arkret producer or Event digest.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte delegation digest or the complete typed content-addressed reference; the reference is the only wire carrier of that digest.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed membership-compensation delegation reference. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(core)) over the profile-defined closed core that carries neither delegation_id nor signature. The delegation object, terminal certificate and single-use CAS token carry only this typed reference; no sibling delegation_digest exists (encoding.md 4.0.1).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7. payload_pattern is the core-registered outer value space the profile MUST stay inside; the profile MAY narrow it further but MUST NOT accept an octet outside it.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32 raw challenge octets together with the challenge consumption ledger row; it is registry-local single-use state, never a federated object ID and never a native UUID column.
special_forms.description: Single-use Organization registration control challenge identifier issued by ak.root.identity.organization_registration.command.prepare.v1. It is registry-allocated, neither content-addressed nor Event-derived, and it never denotes a durable protocol object.

allocation.payload_encoding: 32 octets rendered as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
allocation.uniqueness_rule: The registry MUST atomically reserve the value before returning it and MUST reallocate on any collision with a live or consumed ledger row; a challenge value is never reissued.
allocation.consumption_rule: The registry MUST consume the challenge inside the same transaction that persists (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome).
allocation.replay_rule: Only a byte-identical retry may return the recorded outcome; the same challenge_id carrying any different canonical_request_digest, or a consumed challenge_id with no matching successful ledger row, MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.
allocation.security_rationale: A caller-chosen or request-derived challenge would let the caller pick freshness and defeat single-use consumption, so the registry mints the full 256-bit value itself and binds the outcome to the exact canonical request bytes.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed OrganizationRegistrationReceipt identifier. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims)), where receipt_claims is exactly the receipt object with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted; it is the same content-addressed family as service_registration_receipt and MUST NOT be reused as a Realm capability, membership, governance-Station designation or service delegation.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque install-plan token; do not parse it as UUIDv7.
special_forms.description: Applet install-plan identifier. The suffix is an opaque non-empty base64url token.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Profile-scoped pseudonymous reference. Each consuming profile defines its own scope boundary and narrows the core-registered outer payload_pattern; it MUST NOT accept an octet outside that space. E2EE credential pseudonyms are Realm-scoped, while push pseudonyms are scoped to the registered recipient service, principal, device, route and salt epoch. Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed ServiceRegistrationReceipt identifier derived from canonical receipt claims. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims)).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete typed content-addressed identifier together with the exact canonical signer-evidence bytes.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed authenticated signer-resolution evidence reference. The suffix is the SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical evidence object under its registered digest rule.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical ak:trust_domain:<scope> value by default. A compressed schema may store the raw scope only in an explicitly named trust_domain_scope column and MUST restore the typed prefix at the persistence boundary.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk root, recovery and authorization proofs. NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kind_registry.uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.

notification_projection_identity_contrac.notes: The ID is not a signature or read capability. Verify the original source Event and applicable acceptance evidence, bind the complete recipient AccountId, and rederive the ID. Never rewrite the source Event into account_data.

http_signature_contract_registry.description: Canonical single owner of every RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature contract in Arkret: the shared covered-component baseline, the per-scenario extensions and their trigger conditions, the required signature parameters, and the freshness window numerals. Prose enumerations, conformance profiles and vector descriptions are projections of this block.
registry_rules: Every request required to carry an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature MUST resolve exactly one scenario_id in this registry.

A covered-component set declared here is a MINIMUM, not a closed set: an implementation MAY cover additional components. Verification MUST fail when any applicable required component is absent from Signature-Input.

This registry states set membership only. RFC 9421 keeps the actual ordered component list for base-string construction and for audit records; the order of these arrays carries no protocol requirement and MUST NOT be read as one.
created and expires are RFC 9421 signature parameters. They are never members of a covered-component array.

No operation, prose page, conformance profile, fixture or vector description carries its own covered-set array or window numeral. They cite a scenario_id and project this block; projections are compared by gate, not maintained by hand.
An operation contract binds a scenario through auth_requirements.service_signature.signature_scenario_id and MUST NOT restate covered_components or freshness.
Adding a component to a scenario is a protocol change: the scenario entry, every prose binding block and every declared projection move together or the gate fails.

There is no per-operation deviation mechanism. v1 registers exactly one RFC 9421 freshness profile, and every scenario names it. A surface that genuinely needs a different window is registered as its own scenario with its own profile, prose block and projections, so the deviation carries the same evidence as everything else here. A window numeral that appears only in one page's prose is a defect, not a contract.

component_vocabulary.binds: The HTTP verb, so a signature cannot be replayed on a different method.
The full request target, so a signature cannot be replayed on a different endpoint.
The host, so a signature cannot be replayed against a different deployment.

The exact versioned operation_id this request selected, so the selector cannot be swapped on an already-signed request. Required for every signed canonical request by zh/sync/api-conventions.md section 2.4.1.
The RFC 9530 sha-256 digest of the exact HTTP content bytes.
The idempotency and replay identity of the request.
The requested completion condition, so it cannot be downgraded on a signed request.
The MIMI room the request is scoped to.
The deployment trust domain the request originates from.
The deployment trust domain the request is addressed to, so a cross-domain transaction cannot be replayed into another deployment.
The digest of the addressed service endpoint, so a shared-ingress delivery cannot be replayed onto a different endpoint behind the same ingress.

freshness_profiles.applies_to: RFC 9421 signature parameters created and expires
rules: created and expires MUST both be present as integer UNIX seconds; a missing or non-integer parameter fails.
abs(created - now) <= created_skew_seconds, both bounds inclusive, where now is the receiver current Unix second for this verification.
now < expires. Reaching expires is expiry; expires gets no additional skew grace.
All three checks MUST hold. The replay cache runs independently; cache eviction never excuses a time check or a coverage check.

max_signature_lifetime_seconds caps the lifetime a signature may CLAIM. It is not a promise that a receiver accepts any signature for five minutes: the created skew rule rejects an old signature earlier.

boundary_vector.note: The boundary evidence is bound to operations that actually resolve this profile, not to a profile nobody calls. Two per-operation tightenings were removed in favour of this one window; restoring one, or dropping an operation's scenario binding, changes what these operations resolve and turns this gate red.

freshness_profiles.applies_to: RFC 9449 DPoP proof JWT iat and jti
rules: A DPoP proof carries iat and no expires parameter, so it does not and MUST NOT inherit ak.http_signature.freshness.v1.
Accept only when the receiver current Unix second minus iat lies between minus iat_future_seconds and plus iat_past_seconds, both bounds inclusive.
jti MUST be retained for at least jti_retention_seconds, which MUST be at least iat_past_seconds plus iat_future_seconds, so no still-acceptable proof can be replayed after its jti is forgotten.
A repeated jti inside retention fails closed even when iat is still inside the window.
Sharing one holder key with RFC 9421 does not merge the two contracts; neither profile numerals may be substituted for the other.

protocol_time_tolerance_registry.description: Canonical owner of protocol-level clock-tolerance numerals and of the direction in which each consumer applies them. A tolerance is only a magnitude; each scenario owns its comparison rule, so a one-sided future guard cannot be silently widened into a symmetric grace period.
registry_rules: Every protocol-level clock tolerance MUST be named here with one integer value and one unit. Prose, schemas and fixtures cite a scenario_id and MUST NOT carry a private replacement numeral.

Every scenario MUST select one registered tolerance and one closed direction. future_only applies only to a timestamp later than verification time; symmetric_not_before_and_expiry applies the same magnitude to the future not-before edge and the past expiry edge.

Boundary cases are conjunctive: equality at each declared limit is accepted and one millisecond beyond it is rejected. The fixture is a checked projection of this registry, not a second source of values.
A deployment parameter such as revocation_index_propagation_max_ms is not a protocol clock tolerance and MUST NOT inherit one of these values implicitly.

scenarios.comparison: not_before <= verification_time + tolerance and expires_at >= verification_time - tolerance, both inclusive
issued_at <= verification_time + tolerance and expires_at >= verification_time - tolerance, both inclusive

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise registered supported_operation_bundles and supported_profiles explicitly.

surface_classes and surface_groups are documentation and lint groupings only; no surface tier implies wire reachability. A registered active operation MUST belong to at least one operation bundle advertised by its actual executing endpoint, and an endpoint MUST implement every member of each bundle it advertises.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>.v1. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. kind=branched declares a semantic request discriminator plus a closed effect_branches[] list with unique equals values and one final otherwise branch; each branch contains a complete event_log, actor_private_event, or none leaf effect. An event_log branch that is not unconditional MUST additionally name event_submission_path pointing to the caller-signed EventAdmissionSubmission used by that branch. Field presence is evidence carried by a branch, never the branch discriminator itself. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

Every operation_id is an explicit versioned operation identity ending in .v1. Its stable HTTP endpoint identity is derived by removing the terminal .vN and is used as the OpenAPI operationId; the unversioned identity is not an alias for a versioned operation_id.

Every canonical Arkret HTTP request MUST carry exactly one Arkret-Operation header naming the exact versioned operation_id before body parsing. The receiver MUST verify that the selector is locally advertised and belongs to the selected method/path family and binding. A missing selector fails with operation_selector_required; an empty candidate set, unknown id, duplicate selector, or value outside the route family fails with unsupported_operation_version. Endpoint uniqueness, payload-shape inference, client SDK version, implicit defaults, and version fallback MUST NOT replace the selector. This invariant keeps existing clients stable when another operation version is added to the same HTTP endpoint family.

operation_bundles is the only canonical bundle member source. Each registered bundle freezes one service_kind and a canonical unique set of (operation_id,binding_kind) members; changing a member requires a new bundle id.

coordination_relations is the canonical machine source for a public operation that spans independently durable services. Every relation MUST name the entry operation, every registered sub-operation, exact request/receipt bindings, the durable owner and fence transitions, crash recovery owner, terminal success boundary and closed downstream error translation. Prose alone MUST NOT create an unregistered cross-service write edge.
Within one service_kind, active current-v1 bundles MUST NOT overlap on an identical (operation_id,binding_kind) pair. Pairs using a different binding kind are distinct.

Only registered ak.operation_bundle.*.v1 ids may appear in current-v1 ServiceDescribe. Current-v1 defines no vendor bundle wire namespace; vendor-private collections may only appear as ignorable x_* metadata and never affect capability decisions. Unknown bundle ids fail closed and are never expanded by name.

Request wire/canonical byte budget violations MUST return payload_too_large (HTTP 413); count-only schema violations with valid request bytes MUST return schema_violation (HTTP 422), except explicit operation count semantics. An otherwise valid request whose complete response or evaluation exceeds its semantic budget returns limit_exceeded (HTTP 413) or its defined typed unavailable result. Request byte errors take precedence over coincident schema errors. Error classification MUST NOT depend on diagnostic text substring matching.

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces used for documentation and lint; v1 support does not imply wire reachability without explicit supported_operation_bundles advertisement.
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

service_signature.contract: Covered components, signature parameters and the freshness window come from http_signature_contract_registry. This operation MUST NOT restate them.

delivery_authentication_record.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method and key digest; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id; registration_epoch is the effective destination Applet registration.
delivery_authentication_record.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare did MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. The effective registration_epoch and actual verification key digest are bound. Direct DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.
delivery_authentication_record.equality: Receivers recompute sha256(UTF8(digest_domain + newline) || RFC8785_JCS(record)); equal recomputed digests define replay equality. Caller-supplied records or digests are forbidden.

operations.notes: All directions preserve the unique original producer proof and portable signer authorization. Each receiver verifies exact installation aggregate, scope, grant, epoch and native act-on-behalf authority independently. HTTP source signatures and storage receipts do not authorize Events. The Station-to-Applet authoring_context branch carries the accepted Applet Service signer root plus the managed Actor Principal signer root and its exact Station Service attester leaf; the runtime recomputes and atomically persists all three roots before ordinary authoring. Signals retain their independent proof regime. Original managed PCR resolution updates use the exact original-install native-principal admission of applet-integration.md section 7.3.2.1; Applet HTTP identity never substitutes its producer. Each Account ak:device: committed delivery must carry the immutable original-admission AccountDeviceSignerEvidence sibling; all other producers forbid that member. Verify its original attestation, native Service history, authorization window and Event JWS at the original covering committed_at; later current state does not reinterpret accepted history.

The Applet service consumes the one signed install_applet or provision_ghost authoring request and returns the exact role-neutral four-Event bundle. All four creation Events use the Applet service as actual producer and reference the same real Service AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence root derived from the accepted registration epoch; a pre-effective Bot or Ghost never signs them. Its durable ledger is keyed by branch subject plus full signed-request digest and preserves exact request/bundle bytes, the Service root, actor key handle, method history, and provision state. No derived request ID or branch-specific Event aliases exist.

durable_effect.rationale: The operation admits no Arkret Event; independently, the Applet service atomically persists the subject/request-digest ledger, exact request and bundle, Applet Service signer root, actor key custody, method history, and provision state before returning

operations.notes: HTTP-only authenticated Station-to-Gateway registration handoff for a Station-approved public Gateway. The HTTP Message Signature binds exact Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID and Content-Digest. The Gateway admits only an explicitly onboarded source Station, partitions storage/log/access by that authenticated source, and accepts notify for the installed registration only from that same Station. Each Station-generated registration_id is immutable: exact replay returns the byte-identical signed durable receipt, different content conflicts, revoked is terminal, and an active successor atomically tombstones its exact supersedes_registration_id. The body and receipt carry no AccountId, principal, Realm or user session. Raw provider route material appears only in the active handoff body and the destination tenant's provider adapter, never in notify, receipt, logs, metrics, traces or cross-tenant indexes.

Provided by the push_gateway role. The source service must be authorized by the exact durable registration. For a trusted public-Gateway installation created by ak.edge.push.command.apply_registration.v1, only the exact source Station that installed it may call notify. Notification devices carry only device_id; registration routes and tokens are not supplied by this request.

Provided only by the authenticated AccountId.station_id Station role. The optional station.push bundle contains both registration operations; a push_gateway role does not acquire Account registration authority.

Provided only by the authenticated AccountId.station_id Station role. The optional station.push bundle contains both registration operations; a push_gateway role does not acquire Account registration authority.

Explicit one-step abandonment with a fresh holder-bound account handoff obtained for this confirmation. Validate exact request_id, principal_id, did_version_id, live lease/fence against the durable onboarding checkpoint and confirm PCR was never accepted. The client displays the fixed consequences before sending. Atomically record one orphan tombstone, suppress the checkpoint and release the lease; exact replay returns the same terminal outcome, while an accepted-PCR race returns identity_creation_already_accepted with zero writes.

The one authenticated step that binds an account-less staged pairing record to an exact AccountId (device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1). The caller is the candidate device itself: it holds the exact device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code, holds the staged candidate key, and authenticates with Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP for a bound pending account handoff. That handoff is the sole source of the exact AccountId, which the candidate signs into device_pairing_target_proof; a server-side side channel or an unsigned request member MUST NOT assert account membership. The Account Authority recomputes the 2.1.2 challenge transcript from its own durable stage, verifies the target signature with the staged new_device_pubkey, requires target_proof.account_id to equal the AccountId this handoff is bound to, and only then moves the record from staged to ready_for_claim. The transition is one-way: ready_for_claim never returns to staged and authorized is never reachable without it. Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, an expired record and a record that is no longer staged all return an indistinguishable not_found. Exact retry of the same canonical intent returns the same outcome without re-attaching a proof; the same request id with different content conflicts. Once the request id locates a retained record, a code mismatch, AccountId/handoff mismatch, transcript/signature/proof mismatch or unusable state counts against the Account Authority's service-private ten-failure ledger keyed only by device_pairing_request_id; an unknown id and an exact successful retry do not. The tenth failure atomically expires staged or ready_for_claim, consumes the code and creates the bounded tombstone, while preserving the existing public error shape and creating no Event, authorization, typed current result or success outcome. A successful finalize also supersedes: in the same durable transaction it MUST move every other unaccepted ready_for_claim pending record of that AccountId to terminal expired, keeping the bounded tombstone that preserves exact retry and blocks replay, so the account never holds two approvable records at once. This is what makes the existing MUST NOT in device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1 enforceable, and it is the only way v1 retires the code of an earlier pairing attempt; v1 registers no cancel operation. The supersession key is the AccountId alone, so a refreshed pairing page reusing the same candidate key and a different new device with a fresh candidate key retire the earlier record identically, and adding two new devices in parallel is therefore forbidden. Supersession never authors an Event, grants nothing, and never rewrites the terminal outcome of a record pair_device already accepted; an exact retry performs no second supersession. The durable boundary is the gate-side pending ledger, because only the gate side holds the account binding when the Account Authority is deployed separately from the Station. No Arkret Event is authored and nothing is authorized here.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus did rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve did itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(did)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Station co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, did, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantIntent; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled. If deployment policy permits reactivation and the original account is deactivated, this operation alone atomically authors the deactivated-to-active successor, restores the same account row, creates the publication outbox entry and issues the first new-generation grant. It never creates a replacement account or second PCR, and it never revives an old session, device or KeyPackage; policy denial or incomplete recovery returns account_deactivated with zero authoritative writes.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger SessionGrant issuance with a closed HumanSessionGrantRequest | RecoverySessionGrantRequest | AgentSessionGrantRequest union. OIDC authorization code is never accepted here; authentication-handoffs is the unique code consumer. Returning-human and recovery requests use Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP. Returning-human issuance requires AcceptedDevicePossessionProof and origin revocation-gate allow, consumes the handoff, and emits Standard + complete device_binding. Recovery issuance requires credential_class=recovery_session, binds the account principal/audience, candidate device and handoff DPoP JWK, emits a <=15 minute non-refreshable recovery_candidate_device grant without device_binding, consumes only the request DPoP JTI, and preserves the handoff for recovery completion. Agent issuance keeps its independent agent_key_proof validator. The issuer uses branch-specific request identity and canonical intent to persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. Exact replay is byte-identical; conflict and terminal replay fail closed. The client presents every grant only as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP proof. No Principal Event is authored.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The handler validates the ak.session.grant + DPoP when metadata remains, idempotently terminates the Auth-side auth session / complete grant rotation chain inside the Station TCB when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Exact retries on an already terminal or pruned chain return an equivalent successful no-op; audience mismatch still fails closed. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

One controller-signed authorize Event with inline Ed25519 public_key, exact supersedes and private scope disclosure binds a frozen candidate by pairing_request_id and approval_request_id. The verifier reads its authoritative frozen record (or authenticated verifier-only agent view), independently verifies PoP and candidate, and persists the exact command. Same-candidate PoP refresh does not invalidate approval. Accepted RealmCommit processing automatically activates after rechecking current handle, expiry, candidate, parent authority and activation fence; cancellation or changed authority is terminal. Exact retry returns/reconciles the durable outcome and never revives authority.

The Station TCB owns one pairing ledger.
