Durable terminal exact replay is keyed by pairing request id, approving AccountId/device and canonical request digest and returns the same Event, unique RealmCommit and accepted outcome without a second Event or stage consumption; same identity with changed intent conflicts. On first valid intent the TCB validates current device authority, admits the byte-exact authorize_event once, consumes pending/code once and stores the byte-identical client outcome. A retained request consumes one unit of its service-private ten-failure budget when code, approving AccountId/device, transcript, signature, proof/staged material or ready_for_claim state is invalid; the tenth failure atomically expires an otherwise pending record. Incomplete admission is exempt from ordinary TTL cleanup, failure counting and later finalize supersession, and only the same pair_device intent may resume. Exact terminal replay never counts, and authorized or durable terminal state is never rewritten. Internal transactions, journals, outboxes, RPCs and recovery states are implementation details rather than canonical operations or wire members.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger SessionGrant rotation with a closed HumanSessionGrantRefreshRequest | AgentSessionGrantRefreshRequest union. Both branches present the predecessor as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof and carry no client-generated challenge or generic proof_kind. Human refresh additionally carries AcceptedDevicePossessionProof purpose=session_grant_refresh; the origin verifies it under the locked current accepted-device key and applies the predecessor signed device_binding as expected binding in the same current-authorization linearization. Agent refresh carries only AgentSessionRefreshProof and revalidates current runtime-key authorization/lifecycle through its independent validator. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves subject/scope/audience/cnf.jkt/session_id, and atomically supersedes the predecessor. Exact replay returns the recorded successor; conflicting or terminal replay never issues another. Account/passkey restoration uses a fresh AccountHandoff then issue, and PCR recovery uses its dedicated completion operation; neither is a refresh proof kind. No Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer did and principal_id; every repeated did/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified did, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, registration_anchor_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: The only client entry point for self-initiated account erasure (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface: it authenticates the holder as a high-risk action, durably records the erasure intent and continues its existing erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord issuance flow within the same service — there is no cross-service handoff, because the record issuer, the status-transition legality oracle and the section-8 fanout orchestrator are all the Account Authority, so no 'accepted but issuance pending on another service' intermediate state exists. Authentication freshness is judged locally by the Account Authority, the only party holding recent login / WebAuthn / recovery key facts; a Station MUST NOT determine or approximate it from session-grant introspection or local session state (introspection deliberately projects neither auth_time nor proof kind). The success response is an acceptance confirmation only: the current status is observed through the existing account-status read surface and physical completion only through the erasure receipt rail. The Account Authority MAY insert a deployment-governed withdrawal window (possibly zero) between acceptance and record signing, echoing withdrawal_window_ends_at when one exists; once the erasure_pending record is signed the request is irreversible and any withdrawal MUST fail closed. Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded acceptance outcome; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes; a different request_id while a live unsigned-record intent exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending. A session that does not satisfy the deployment's fresh high-risk action authentication policy is rejected with reauthentication_required.

Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Unique current-v1 OIDC authorization-code consumer. Account Authority exchanges and validates the code and issues an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key plus the deployment-local stable account_subject. The external callback receiver that owns the redirect transaction validates state; Account Authority validates state only when it owns that transaction, and always validates issuer, token exchange/PKCE, redirect_uri and ID Token nonce. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy. Bound clients normalize local evidence before choosing returning issue, pairing-first Device Setup or diagnostics; identity onboarding accepts only the other two states. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. When deployment policy allows reactivation, fresh account authentication may return a bound recovery-candidate handoff for the original deactivated account, but the handoff does not change status and ordinary register, issue and refresh remain blocked; only recovery completion may reactivate it. Policy denial returns account_deactivated with zero recovery writes.

Authenticated retrieval of one pending pairing request by its normalized eight-character code, so a desktop browser with no camera can join a device by typing the code shown on the new device (device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1). The caller is a current accepted, non-pending-revocation device of an exact AccountId and the code is the whole input; it MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. Before locating any code, the Account Authority MUST verify an active Standard human SessionGrant plus exact HTTP DPoP/JTI, apply the caller-device/AccountId/service transport buckets, and obtain a fresh matching private current-device decision using both expected selectors from the signed device_binding. SessionGrant is only a selector source, never the current-state authority. Any non-allow, unavailable, mismatched or expired gate result fails closed before pairing lookup and consumes no per-request failure budget, with behavior independent of whether the submitted code exists. The service returns the resolved bootstrap and the byte-equivalent target proof only when the code then hits a unique unexpired ready_for_claim unconsumed request in the Account Authority's single gate-side pending ledger whose signed account_id and gate audience equal the caller's own account, and when proof, staged key, request id, code and transcript digest all agree. Unknown, wrong, expired, superseded, cross-account, not yet finalized and already consumed codes MUST all return the same not_found, so an error shape never says whether a code exists or which account it belongs to. The response carries no private key, no session credential, no recovery material and nothing about any other device of the account. Claiming retrieves a request and grants nothing: the accepted device still has to review it and sign ak.device.authorize. A code that cannot locate an exact retained request creates no per-request counter row; once it does locate one, an AccountId/gate/proof/staged-material or usable-state failure counts against the Account Authority's service-private ledger keyed by device_pairing_request_id. Attempts one through nine keep pending state unchanged; the tenth atomically expires and consumes it without changing the uniform not_found response.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime submits one candidate with an Ed25519 PoP over the authoritative handle, eight-digit decimal pairing code, service DID, stable raw-key binding and at-most-five-minute window. Same-binding retries refresh the verified PoP while preserving candidate/approval/notification identity; different candidate on one handle conflicts. Controller signs the inline-key authorize Event once; approval is independent of PoP refresh. Secret and proof occur only in request body and confidential verifier material.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries the authorized key binding plus current_signer_evidence and signer_resolution_evidence_ref. The runtime compares authorized_public_key_digest against its own key, independently verifies and rebuilds the signer evidence/ref, persists that closure, and then authors Events offline; authorized_event_ref never substitutes for signer_resolution_evidence_ref. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state staged. The pairing_code MUST be unique across the whole live pending set of the service, because it is also the sole lookup key of the authenticated code claim; a user-driven refresh is simply another call to this operation and mints a distinct request and code; the earlier record is closed not here but by the next successful finalize for that AccountId, and a record still in staged is harmless because resolve, code claim and pair_device all require ready_for_claim. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing: the account binding happens one step later, at the authenticated ak.gate.account.command.finalize_device_pairing.v1. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. Only a record that has already been finalized to ready_for_claim can be resolved; resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a record that is not ready_for_claim so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state staged before finalize and ready_for_claim after it; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. A record superseded by a later successful ak.gate.account.command.finalize_device_pairing.v1 for the same AccountId reports the same expired during that retention period and is indistinguishable from a naturally elapsed TTL; the query credential is the request id plus the pairing code, so only the candidate device that minted the record can observe it and no prior existence is disclosed. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the current public principal resolution projection from the known Station. The response carries only the account pair, the projection, bounded adapter method evidence and the Station projection attestation; it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted RealmCommit. Account-internal audit material moved to ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1, so this surface has no history selector. This is a second-hop projection fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, verify the attestation proof under the current station_id method history, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(did)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The authenticated Provider-ID scopes the canonical full-body hash. The service atomically binds that key to the service-authored Event and Commit; exact retry returns the same result, while a proof reused with different claim bytes is rejected.

Observer role is rejected before Event construction, durable state, receipt or fanout. MIMI group identity is checked against verified RFC 9420 public group material and the sole group-id derivation from current accepted MlsGroupCurrent.effective_scope; the five-field governance binding carries no group id.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventAdmissionSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through authority Event submission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

discriminator.description: The caller-declared semantic MIMI update kind. The decoded opaque payload MUST carry the same kind before a branch is admitted.

operations.notes: Return a nonce-bound genesis-to-current authority chain; locators are hints and never authority.

Returns current AuthenticatedServiceResolution containing service_id, service_kind, complete method_history_evidence and normalized_did_document. Consumers independently verify method-native history, current state, service identity/type, unique canonical HTTPS DID service endpoint and second-hop describe binding. Durable native method state prevents rollback and fork; cache TTL is at most 300 seconds and failed freshness checks never extend it. Endpoint refresh does not require Realm rebind; a changed service core requires a new authorized binding.

Back-binding activation of one provisioned private record to exactly one accepted ak.invite.third_party (third-party-invites.md section 7.5). The body carries provisioning_id and the Station-signed ThirdPartyInviteAcceptanceAttestation; the attestation is the whole authorization, so a caller-reported invite id, a caller-computed invite digest, an Event signature or an HTTP success MUST NOT be accepted in its place. The service verifies the Station service identity and signature, audience, exact verification_id, the attestation's signed expires_at/invite_expires_at bounds, and member-for-member equality of author, Realm, expiry and public material against the frozen provisioning record, recomputes invite_digest from the attested typed current result per section 4.2, then atomically persists the unique binding and the delivery intent. One provisioning record binds to one invite forever: a second attestation naming a different invite, Realm or author is refused and never rebinds, rotates the key or reissues the token. A byte-identical retry, a concurrent duplicate and a retry after a restart all return the original binding.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Delivery to an external mail or SMS gateway cannot be recalled. The intent MUST be durable before success is returned, and the delivered material stays the one invite this activation bound; stopping an already delivered invite requires an authorized writer's ak.invite.revoke.

operations.notes: Token presentation surface of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 4.1). The invitee's client submits invite_token, realm_id, subject_account_id, subject_did and a client claim_nonce in the JSON body; the service validates token, expiry, claim count and Realm binding, atomically consumes the token, signs the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript with the invite's verification_public_key and returns invite_id, token_commitment and binding_proof. invite_token in the URL query string or path segment is rejected with third_party_invite_token_in_query and the token SHOULD be invalidated; a knock_restricted Realm is rejected with unsupported_join_rule; every other failure is non-enumerable (section 6). A consumed token MUST NOT be re-bound to a different subject; the same (realm_id, subject_account_id, claim_nonce) MAY be answered with the same binding_proof inside the recoverable window (section 6.1).

Private-material provisioning entry of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 7.2). An authenticated inviter submits request_id, realm_id, inviter_account_id, verification_id, oob_code_kind, the private mailto:/tel: delivery target and the requested expiry, signed under ak.third_party_invite_provision_request_proof.v1 with the service DID as audience. The service mints and durably keeps the token, the per-invite 256-bit token_salt or lookup pepper and the per-invite ephemeral signing key, then returns only the public third_party_invite object, the effective expires_at, the activation deadline and an opaque provisioning_id. It MUST NOT return the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key or the delivery target, MUST NOT create a pending Realm Invite, MUST NOT mint an invite_id and MUST NOT deliver anything before activation. Same request_id plus byte-identical canonical intent replays the original outcome; same request_id plus different intent is duplicate_conflict with no second set of material. An unimplemented oob_code_kind or delivery scheme is unsupported_feature; every existence failure stays non-enumerable (section 6).

Lifecycle and out-of-band delivery position of one provisioning record (third-party-invites.md section 7.6). provisioning_id is the whole query credential and MUST travel only in the JSON body. It is the recovery surface after a lost provisioning or activation response and the only standard delivery observation point. The outcome carries provisioning_state, and once activated also invite_id, activated_at, delivery_state and delivery_attempt_count; it MUST NOT carry the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key, delivery target or any 3PID-derived value, and MUST NOT reveal whether the invitee opened the invite. An unknown handle, a handle belonging to another inviter and a deleted record MUST be indistinguishable.

Replicates one exact Account Authority-signed AccountStatusRecord. The receiver verifies transport authentication, record identity/proof, exact account/principal/binding tuple, sequence continuity and previous_account_status_record_id, then atomically advances its monotonic replica and emits a signed receipt. A gap returns dependency_missing with zero writes; stale, duplicate and fork are distinguished without rebuilding or re-signing the record. For status=erasure_pending, accepted or duplicate is returned only after a durable physical-erasure intent keyed by receiver service, account, triggering record and storage boundary exists. Same Idempotency-Key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: The signed record is the only erasure command. Acceptance is forbidden until the receiver has a durable execution intent; physical completion is established only by a verified ErasureReceiptPackage.

operations.notes: Service-authenticated bounded read of a contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range for freshness and replica gap recovery. The Account Authority returns original signed records in status_seq order and never exposes an account to a service without an existing exact account/principal relationship. Empty, unknown and unauthorized are non-enumerating at the operation boundary.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, or bilateral continuity-checkpoint control. Authorizing source receipts, directional proofs and the receipted outbox exist only after the exact source command unit is RealmCommit-committed and its effects atomically installed. The receiver verifies the independently derived source Station's historical service attestation and original holder producer separately; no private PCR bootstrap or generic authority-commit proof disclosure is added, and source_checkpoint is not a RealmCommit. The continuity branch carries a one-sided proposal; the receiver recomputes the exact core, verifies the proposer signature, appends only its own participant service-authority signature, durably commits the complete checkpoint and returns it with a signed control receipt. Exact replay returns the same bytes; same-sequence different-digest forks fail closed. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. The original source-signed Event receipt or lineage includes the exact producer_signer method and Ed25519 raw32 key. This permits the first Contact carrier without an existing relationship or private PCR disclosure; it is an exact-Event producer projection, not reusable Control or device authority. The delegated producer projection is structurally defined but v1 Contact commands MUST reject controller-device Agent holder submissions until an exact holder selector is registered; human and Agent-runtime branches forbid it. This complete Agent public DID locator is frozen from verified native identity, rechecked against the exact Actor/controller/Station, and grants no authority.

Service-authenticated terminal erasure-result fanout only; it never requests or triggers deletion. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. The receiver verifies the closed trigger union, receipt, issuer authority, every proof, receipt_digest and exact retained-stub binding before durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. Account erasure requires the account_status_record trigger branch to equal the accepted erasure_pending record; other erasure uses the event branch.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

The sole peer Event ingress is a closed semantic union. authority_forward sends one exact producer Event or MLS Commit to the verified current governance Station, which alone may sign a new RealmCommit; an ak.mls.genesis Event additionally carries mls_genesis_material, the raw bytes of the two content-addressed Blobs it references, which the governance Station hashes against the refs and stores in the acceptance transaction, and every other kind omits it. committed_replication carries replications[1..100] whose rows are {event_submission, source_commit}, plus required immutable genesis_event_ref for every ak.mls.commit and forbidden for every other kind; only a Commit may additionally carry welcomes[] of recipients hosted by the destination. The governance Station freezes the Genesis ref from its accepted group provenance in the Commit acceptance transaction and the authenticated canonical peer request signature covers it. The receiver binds it to the exact Commit and immutable group provenance in the replica transaction, re-verifies Welcomes against its own claim ledger and queues passing Welcomes in that same transaction; it never infers Genesis from a preceding Commit ref or current tree. Processing, committed_event wrappers, sender membership witnesses, destination echoes and response coordinate echoes are absent. The receiver derives authorization from verified committed history and stores exact source facts without first admission, re-signing, or second fanout. registered_atomic_unit carries only registered all-or-nothing source-committed units (Direct Conversation founding or membership compensation), never per-item partial materialization. canonical_hash/full_body binds the complete selected branch and exact replay returns the original branch outcome. Exact full-request replay preserves the first outcome bytes, item order and stored status. duplicate describes initial processing under a different full request whose exact source Event/Commit already exists; it is not a replacement status for a replayed stored outcome. authority_forward registers producer_agent_evidence exactly for actual Agent runtime producers, independently of outer actor_id; human/device and service producers forbid it. Compact requires a fully verified exact state_digest cache, otherwise dependency_missing. Restored complete evidence is retained atomically with first admission; it never grants participation current.

discriminator.description: Closed peer ingress semantic branch. Schema validation proves that final otherwise can only be registered_atomic_unit.

effect.rationale: Only the verified current governance Station performs first admission and signs the new RealmCommit.

operations.notes: Replicate one visibility-authorized stream from its current governance Station. Full digest-bearing Human rows carry original Commit-bound immutable facts; original source Ed/coordinates/time are verified and atomically retained, including bootstrap tail and cold backfill. No PCR history or current-key reconstruction.

Private Station to Station invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.account_id.station_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee_account_id equals invite_address.account_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Atomic cross-Station KeyPackage claim. The destination Station is the sole atomic claim-ledger authority for its KeyPackage inventory. The authenticated source Station first validates the participant request against its exact local account/device/generation durable state; revocation_pending fails before any remote call or inventory disclosure and is exposed only as the existing opaque claim_failed result. Request and response carry no PCR/control-history or separate signer-evidence sidecar. Every claim binds the matching accepted authorization Event id plus the signed destination claim receipt, exact selectors and KeyPackage signature; the destination checks the target against its local PCR (or local Agent current authorization) at the claim cut, and the requester verifies a device-branch signer through the peer directory attestation (purpose mls_group_admission) whose device_authorize_event_id and signing key match the claim record and KeyPackage signature, or an Agent-branch signer through its Agent signer evidence. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and the canonical request digest.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read, the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target. requester_account_id.station_id equals the authenticated Source-Service-ID and every target account_id.station_id equals the Destination-Service-ID; no client SessionGrant, DPoP or local bearer is ever forwarded and clients never call this surface. The destination completes transport authentication before any target read, then re-derives the declared relationship from its own accepted state: realm_membership requires both parties to be current effective joined members of that exact Realm, while contact reads only the target's own current outbound Contact scope and never requires a shared Realm. Purpose is authorized independently. Absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets collapse into an omitted row or device_result_unavailable, rate limited per requester and per target. Rows carry the origin's own attestation and signer evidence ref; the destination adds no response signature. Request <=64 KiB with 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each; complete response <=512 KiB, no continuation. Cross-Station single-use material remains the MLS KeyPackage claim contract.

service_signature.contract: Covered components, signature parameters and the freshness window come from http_signature_contract_registry. This operation MUST NOT restate them.

operations.notes: Recipient Account Station submits its durable signed exact-Commit Add authority attestation after existing committed-replication claim verification. Governance Station installs it only against frozen accepted Proposal provenance; identical replay returns duplicate, conflicting bytes fail closed. This is not Commit admission and creates no Event.

service_signature.contract: Covered components, signature parameters and the freshness window come from http_signature_contract_registry. This operation MUST NOT restate them.

operations.notes: Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. A self member forwarding request also binds caller_actor_id and target Commit/epoch; governance checks that exact Actor's current and target-cut membership/history and the calling Station's replication right at the target accepted Commit cut. Without caller_actor_id this remains Station replication-only and checks the Station's replication right at the Genesis Commit position. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every selector, hashes raw bytes against content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Current governance Station returns one signed page of a complete historical MLS roster only to the caller Actor's authenticated Account Station, after both current-head and target-cut member/history gates. Every signed page manifest carries the two immutable public Blob refs from the exact accepted Genesis so a later-joined member can construct the separate material read without crossing its history floor. Each Add record carries the exact attestor Station's complete historical authenticated service resolution frozen with its verified receipt and attestation; the signed full-record digest binds that closure. Pages hold the longest continuous prefix of 1..8 complete records fitting the 2 MiB canonical response limit, with a cut-bound cursor naming the next record. Missing Genesis refs, Add attestation, attestor resolution or changing cut, and a single record that cannot fit, are uniformly unavailable, never a partial list. The peer service signature is mandatory and each page repeats the same signed manifest. Governance budgets both this page and its exact self_roster_read_outcome key projection within 2 MiB; the Account Station must verify inline method history itself, not blindly proxy a verified label. A retained Commit signer never authorizes first live discovery.

service_signature.contract: Covered components, signature parameters and the freshness window come from http_signature_contract_registry. This operation MUST NOT restate them.

operations.notes: Install a planned dual-signed authority handoff after complete snapshot and all stream heads are imported.

Initial closed join intent or opaque continuation cursor; freeze the unique confirmed Realm head and exact request identity, recheck intent and each object scope disclosure authorization on every page/replay. Typed RealmCommit/Event/governance dependency/applicant predecessor pages; full independent replay before authoring. Required but undisclosable private-scope material fails with revision_unavailable. An invite grants no private Circle read authority. 8 MiB per page, never a total history cap.

Pre-join preview answered only by the current governance Station of realm_id. The caller is the requester's own Station using service-to-service authentication and never forwards the requester's local bearer or session credential; requester_account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and the holder MUST be the Destination-Service-ID. With invite_id the holder requires that invite in its accepted current state to be live and bound to the complete requester_account_id; without invite_id it evaluates the non-invited audience. It discloses only what the effective ak.realm.preview_policy permits for that audience. A valid target whose policy discloses nothing returns the minimal public_preview; unknown Realm, a holder that is not the current governance Station, an unknown, mismatched or terminal invite, a wrong source and an absent preview policy share one non-enumerating not_found under a fixed timing bucket. The outcome carries no authority bundle, is not membership and discloses no history, roster or policy text.
Transient encrypted Signal rail. It creates no durable Event or RealmCommit, does not advance any authority stream, and grants no delivery or authorization proof.

service_signature.contract: Covered components, signature parameters and the freshness window come from http_signature_contract_registry. This operation MUST NOT restate them.

operations.notes: The wrapper carries one DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, did, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, governance-Station authority, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and did and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core did refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No did is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with did, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published did and signed receipt, with project(did)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

The configured Account Station provides verified public identity resolution to its clients through this standard operation. Clients bind the exact DID/subject/purpose to their trusted Station context without fetching method history. A server or independent verifier admitting external resolver material validates the native method evidence and historical authority; remote self-assertions are not trusted. Registration before an Account session requires the expected authenticated registration service/issuer binding. Requested evidence must be derived from verified state or fail closed.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventAdmissionSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control RealmCommit MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before RealmCommit materialization it returns retry-safe revision_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Creates one durable recovery session owned by the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt presented as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP. request_id, canonical create intent, candidate device, principal, audience and grant coordinates are immutable. Same request identity plus identical intent returns the retained session; a different intent or reuse of one grant for another session fails duplicate_conflict.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Requires the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt frozen by create. Proof transcript binds request_id, grant id, cnf.jkt and the complete recovery session tuple. Exact proof replay returns the retained verified outcome; another proof intent after terminal transition fails closed.

Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) registration key. The client supplies did plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=did, projects did to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventAdmissionSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact account-local PCR Realm selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through authority Event submission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Success exists only after the current PCR governance Station atomically accepts the Event, writes the actor_profile typed current result and signs the returned RealmCommit. Exact retry returns the byte-identical stored outcome and the same Commit. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no account-local-lineage selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Bounded account long polling with independently paged Realm summaries, at most 16 selected Realm details, five segmented global baselines, explicit filter replacement and durable cursor recovery. Empty Realm selection returns no detail. Current authorization and invalidation channels are never window-filtered. Canonical frame <=8 MiB; a round <=16 MiB and <=16 frames; see client-sync section 2.3. HTTP filter and realm_list each use one percent-encoded RFC 8785 JSON query value, preserving empty objects/arrays; dotted/deepObject aliases are not accepted. agent_draft_pending_intents is an independent controller-holder-private baseline/delta channel with its own projection position, frozen cut, offsets and completion marker; it never reuses account_data.events, account_data.station_cas, notifications or to_device. notifications.items is one closed union discriminated by id form: ak:notification:<uuidv7> is the Agent runtime approval branch and ak:notification_projection:<token> is the ordinary source-Event current row, sharing one projection position, one notifications baseline channel and the same per-frame budget. Ordinary rows carry no inbox state and are re-authorized on every frame, frozen baseline pages included; there is no second notification list operation. See client-sync sections 2.3, 3.1 and 3.3.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private typed current result subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_server_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. expected_revision is not accepted as an alias. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_server_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_server_revision + 1. expected_revision is not accepted as an alias or second field. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Accepts exactly one caller-signed actor-private Event whose kind is ak.device.push_route, ak.agent.action_request, ak.agent.action_reject or ak.agent.draft.propose; ak.account_data.set and ak.read_cursor.advance keep their dedicated operations. The authenticated caller MUST be the Event's actual signing actor, and the AccountId selected by the kind's storage_owner.account_id_source MUST belong to this Station, otherwise param_invalid with zero writes. The service validates the exact Event bytes, never rebuilds the payload or co-signs, and in one private transaction evaluates the kind's registered concurrency, writes its value projection and records the exact-retry ledger row (zh/models/actor-private-effects.md section 2). The write produces no RealmCommit and enters no commit stream. The outcome is discriminated by event_kind; ak.device.push_route also returns the accepted revision. An exact retry of the same canonical Event bytes returns the first stored outcome; the same event_id with different bytes is duplicate_conflict, a push_route revision mismatch is cas_conflict, and a missing, terminal, expired or otherwise unwritable target is failed_precondition, all with zero writes.

discriminator.description: The kind of the submitted actor-private Event; each branch writes only that kind's registered private effect.

operations.notes: Only outward carrier for the PCR-resident ak.profile.create / ak.profile.update facts. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through a Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector on ak.self.committed_event.read.scan.v1. Authorization is current effective joined membership of body realm_id for both the caller and each returned actor; realm_id MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm. Each row returns the display projection, one exact signed profile Event and the exact RealmCommit that accepted it; the service and caller verify event_ref, PCR stream, authority generation and signature. The authenticated own-Station projection is not independently proven complete by that pair; a patch Event alone cannot reconstruct the full profile. It grants no authority and exposes no other PCR Event. Unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, missing committed provenance, non-member actor and unauthorized caller all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot probe membership or account existence.
Controller-only bearer+DPoP; Agent runtime is forbidden. Runtime consumes authenticated session participation overlay only, never as action-time current.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record. Controller-only bearer+DPoP; Agent runtime is forbidden. Runtime consumes authenticated session participation overlay only, never as action-time current.

Authenticated controller view. The Station that owns the pairing candidate is the single owner of the raw PoP material and verifies it there; the Account Authority consumes the authenticated exact outcome and does not read verifier-only raw material through this operation. No generic account impersonation or caller-selected candidate is allowed.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

The four creation Events carry one real Applet Service signer-evidence ref. The successful transaction durably retains that exact Service root with the Event set and install state. Once the managed Actor resolution projection is accepted, completion atomically materializes and retains its Principal root plus the exact Station Service attester leaf and enqueues the existing authoring_context delivery; runtime signer inputs are not mirrored into the administrator outcome.

Before the first domain effect, the Station recomputes the canonical AppletRevokePlan and verifies every caller-signed capability revoke against the plan's grant_id, expected_revision, registration_epoch and reason_code. A plan mismatch or stale capability CAS produces no new domain effect and requires a new preview, user confirmation and signature. Exact response-loss retries replay the persisted signed bytes; neither client nor Station rewrites expected_revision.

The active Applet service submits only Realm, exact external tuple, and optional display input. The Station derives every current registration, grant, registration-epoch, package, hosting, and time coordinate, atomically supersedes any prior uncommitted generation for the same branch subject, and returns the exact persisted signed authoring request.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Station durably records the current subject generation and exact signed request before returning

operations.notes: All four creation Events use the Applet Service as actual producer and carry its real Service signer-evidence ref; the pre-effective Ghost never signs this unit. Commit durably retains that root with the four Events and Ghost state. Completion atomically materializes the Ghost Principal root and exact Station Service attester leaf and enqueues the existing authoring_context delivery; the synchronous outcome does not mirror runtime signer inputs.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Station atomically persists the branch-subject winner, exact unsigned payload, exact signed request, and superseded generations before returning

operations.notes: Each capability revoke intent atomically pairs an active Grant selected from the exact Applet install with that same capability_grant current result's expected_revision. The revision is a required canonical plan member covered by the caller-computed revoke_plan_digest and must be copied unchanged into the signed CapabilityRevokePayload. Grant ids, create Event ids, Realm heads, list digests and locally folded state are not revision carriers.

Query parameters are realm_id, optional subject_actor_id and optional at. subject_actor_id is a percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId, including Account and Service branches. Omission selects the authenticated credential's exact ActorId. subject_actor_id is the only accepted subject parameter, so subject, subject_station_id and subject_account_id are invalid; no principal-only, local-service, bearer-service, DID-document or inferred-routing fallback is allowed. Each returned EffectiveCapabilityGrantRow MUST atomically pair one active effective CapabilityGrant with the exact revision of that same capability_grant current result. That row revision is the only relinquish authoring basis; state_digest, evaluated_at, Event ids and locally folded history MUST NOT substitute. Unauthorized, missing and terminal grants remain non-enumerating. A query carrying at is evaluation-only and MUST be refreshed without at before authoring. After refresh or cas_conflict a client MUST obtain explicit user reconfirmation before signing against the newly read revision.

Optional query realm_id and cursor. Explicit subject and subject_station_id MUST be paired did_core_id values identifying an exact AccountId. Omitting both selects only the authenticated credential's exact AccountId. Handles, principal-only requests and inferred Station fallbacks are forbidden; self authorization compares the entire AccountId.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through authority Event submission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_id, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; the Circle scope stays plaintext until its own ak.mls.genesis is accepted.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id and the complete target ActorId is payload.member_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission. Path actor_id is one percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId segment, not a bare principal DID; it is a route selector and does not rename the Event field. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed expected_revision guard; payload.circle_id MUST equal its path identifier and payload.member_id MUST equal the entire decoded path ActorId, including Station and branch. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). The circles array contains full CircleView for Circle members and the fixed CirclePreview for parent-Realm members when directory_visibility=realm_members; invisible Circles are omitted.

Reads a full CircleView for joined Circle members, or fixed CirclePreview for joined parent-Realm non-members when directory_visibility=realm_members and state=active. Invisible and absent Circles have the same not_found envelope.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Event carried in grant_event through authority Event submission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated typed current result subject and the security-set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (the exact current authority-root controller; root_control_only forbids independent controller/Agent delegation).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent typed current result. On admission the recipient Station writes one holder-private ak.account.holder_quarantine entry with surface_kind consent_request, carrying no Event ref and none of the invite_delivery branch members; it shares the invite delivery quota, ledger and CAS chokepoint. Because this operation declares no idempotency key and carries no nonce, that branch deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness over (account_id, source_peer_principal_id, consent_scope). The written entry is holder-private service-local material, so durable_effect stays none.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Event carried in revoke_event through authority Event submission. The payload identifies exactly one stable consent_id and expected_revision; the governing Station performs an atomic current-row CAS and sets that Consent to revoked. No grant dots or revoked_event_refs exist. An any-scope Consent is independent: revoking it does not cascade to concrete-scope Consent rows; clients that intend to revoke multiple rows must sign one exact-revision Event per consent_id.
Lists holder-private consent typed results for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive typed current result state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.

Reads one holder-private consent typed current result only when the authenticated holder has exactly one exact peer match after optional consent_scope filtering. Zero matches use the existing resource-absent response; multiple matches fail with failed_precondition. Peers never receive this DTO; callers needing a specific consent_id use the holder-private list.

Holder-authorized deterministic compaction of the oldest contiguous terminal Contact prefix. The server computes the core from accepted history; callers cannot submit or choose it. Cross-service pairs use the continuity_checkpoint branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1: the receiver recomputes, countersigns, durably commits and returns the complete checkpoint in one round trip, then the proposer commits the exact returned bytes. Exact replay returns the same checkpoint; same sequence with another digest is continuity_invalid and has no winner. Export reuses continuity_evidence on ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 and import reuses the Contact request continuity_evidence field.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. The same trust domain and exact ActorId pair cannot reset its lineage or founding slot. Missing continuity must be recovered or explicitly imported; a full tail without a bilateral checkpoint stays blocked. Only an explicitly initiated first contact for a legally different exact ActorId pair creates an independent root, without inherited checkpoint, history, audit identity, DM or MLS state.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1 operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Authenticated holder projection from server-verified durable Contact evidence. pending_incoming includes request_event_ref and the exact optional request_message; respond/reject use peer and request_event_ref. Complete continuity_evidence is exported only for explicit boolean query include_continuity=true (default false); online recontact uses Station durable checkpoint and bounded tail. Private Consent and account-data notes are not Contact authority. Accepted human rows may carry peer_endpoint{contact_event_ref,device_id} mechanically derived from the verified peer producer receipt of the selected current Contact round; other states and Agent rows forbid it. Missing source omits the projection. Reload, another holder device and glare use the same durable projection; current KeyPackage claim and MLS governance still authorize Add, never this historical selector. No peer PCR read or device enumeration.

Authenticated exact AccountId selects its unique accepted PCR and current PrincipalResolutionProjection, independent of optional profile. Before the first accepted RealmCommit, only the exact atomically accepted genesis current is eligible while no accepted resolution successor exists; derived cache metadata is not authority. The own Station validates method history; no portable evidence or observation time is returned. Wrong or invisible account returns not_found; unresolved verified current state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Authenticated non-enumerating read of exactly one closed Relation primary_conflict_domain or moderation_state target_ref selector from the current governing Station. The outcome binds realm_id, governance_generation, effective_stream_head and either one selector-identical present entry or an affirmative never_written selector from the same durable cut. never_written may supply expected_revision=null only for Relation create; moderation lift and Relation update/tombstone require present. Invisible, foreign, unknown and unauthorized selectors all return the same not_found and MUST NOT return never_written. Unavailable authority, incomplete coverage, timeout, stale generation, snapshot omission and holder-local history prove no absence. Consumers verify selector equality, Realm/stream binding, current governance generation and revision not ahead of the effective head before authoring; CAS conflict requires a new read, user confirmation and signature. Agent interaction also accepts the exact agent_interaction selector with complete agent_account_id; authorized same-cut never_written permits an omitted expected_revision first mode write and confirmed private default. A guessed ID is not disclosure authority. Mode reads do not expose private participation selection or authorize interaction. Original issuers may also read an exact capability_grant selector for their owned_agent grants, including ineffective and terminal rows and the exact CAS revision. No grant never_written or third-party disclosure. See authz/owned-agent-authority.md section 4.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic recipient-delivery acknowledgement for one authenticated human-device or Agent-runtime endpoint (client-sync.md §10.1). The token covers one ordered queue containing both DeviceMessageEnvelope and MlsWelcomeDelivery branches; only this operation prunes it. Account stream and list cursors are read-only. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_account_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1. Full endpoint capacity returns universal quota_exceeded before any batch queue or idempotency write; it never evicts an unacknowledged DeviceMessage or Welcome.

Reads the authenticated recipient endpoint's single ordered private queue. Each deliveries[] item is a closed device_message or mls_welcome branch; the same queue position, read-only cursor and cumulative ACK token span both. Human devices may also receive these items in account delta; Agent runtimes use their own current authorized endpoint and MUST NOT borrow a controller/device queue. See client-sync.md §10.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists. Found MUST include coordinates.binding_event_ref naming an accepted endorsement for authoring. Clients trust their own Station current result and exact committed proposal decision; they do not replay a governance history closure.

Submit an exact producer-signed Event, MLS Commit, ordinary Realm bootstrap unit, Direct Conversation founding unit, or membership compensation unit to the current governance Station. Ordinary bootstrap uses the registered ordered slots in one Realm stream and one all-or-nothing storage transaction; success and exact replay return the same consecutive source RealmCommits without a batch-level receipt. Direct Conversation founding is its own ordered four-Event all-or-nothing unit with a separate founding-slot fence; success and exact replay return the same four consecutive source RealmCommits, whose fourth committed_at is the sole acceptance time. No founding receipt exists. Compensation carries closed transport-only evidence and a single-use CAS. canonical_hash/full_body remains the operation replay identity for every branch; no arbitrary atomic Event batch is admitted. An Event whose kind has wire_scope actor_private_event is refused with unsupported_event_kind and zero writes; it is submitted only through its dedicated actor-private operation.

Return the complete durable frozen fanout target set for one caller-visible accepted Event. Unknown and invisible Events share not_found. Rows use stable opaque target_id and are sorted byte-wise; service_id is included only when the caller can currently read an exact contributing joined-member ActorId routing projection. The query has no retry, route-resolution or delivery state side effect.
Read one authorized Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream by continuous stream_position.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted RealmCommit covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact account_id; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. account_id is server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Station. invite_event_id must resolve to an Event already accepted by this service and authored by the current session actor. The service reads its own stored canonical Event bytes; local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path and remote delivery builds the peer request from those bytes.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over.
