While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.
Issue a durable current-device-only challenge with lifetime at most 300 seconds. Recovery unlock reuses its recovery session challenge.
Same still-authorized holder exact replay returns the durable unlock outcome without charging the one-use challenge again.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the same empty success response, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Station's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Station verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current joined-member ActorId routing projection; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Read-only recipient-side resolution of one keypackage_claim_ref before a Welcome is decrypted. The caller's authenticated endpoint must be the exact endpoint of the claim record (human device: complete AccountId and device_id; Agent: agent_id with its current verification method and ak.agent.key.authorize Event). The response is the byte-identical keypackages_claim_outcome serialized when the claim request was first admitted (claim_request_id, every claims[] row and the destination-signed claim_receipt), never re-signed or trimmed, so the recipient recomputes claims_digest and verifies the receipt against its own Station. Unknown, foreign, superseded-Agent and retention-expired claims are one keypackage_unknown. It changes no claim or KeyPackage state.

Authenticated cross-account device directory and published prekey-bundle read. Selectors are bounded at 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each with a 64 KiB canonical request; an over-limit request fails whole. Disclosure requires a current authorization relationship - a Realm the requester still joins, or a current Contact/call/session context, where the Contact case never requires a shared Realm. Targets hosted by another Station are resolved through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 and verified locally before the row is returned; the client never contacts a foreign Station and its session credential is never forwarded. failures[].reason_code is the closed pair device_result_unavailable and device_directory_unavailable, and an unavailable fetch is never rendered as an empty device set.

Own-Station verified route and signing keys for the media service anchored by one joined Realm current accepted realm_media_service typed current result. Membership visibility and the anchored typed current result are evaluated under one confirmed basis with exactly one head per Realm; the caller supplies no service id, DID, base URL or candidate origin. The result resolves service identity, purpose and route only: it releases no media key, no backend token and no plaintext-visibility authorization, and expires_at bounds route and key reuse to at most 300 seconds. Invisible Realm or absent anchor returns not_found; unresolved accepted state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and complete response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Prepare one complete unsigned ak.message.create from a closed intent, after client encryption where required. Exact canonical request replay; expires at client created_at plus 300 seconds. No sequence reservation and no submit ticket.

durable_effect.rationale: Only a bounded expiring preparation cache; no accepted Event, sequence, membership or projection mutation.

operations.notes: Carries one caller-signed moderation report Event. The current governance Station revalidates the authenticated reporter, target visibility, effective scope and current authorization, then commits the exact Event on that scope's authority stream. The Event contains only its closed producer, scope, payload and signature fields.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or co-sign. The cursor object carries neither an id nor an updated_at — a cursor is never updated in place, its identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple and there is no read_cursor typed ID kind — so the update time of an advance is the Event envelope created_at, and the read_marker_outcome updated_at is that derived envelope time of the winning advance. Sibling devices observe the winner as the ak.read_cursor.update device message whose content is ak.schema.read_cursor_update.v1. Multi-device convergence follows zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position committed on the same CommitStreamRef with the larger stream_position wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only when neither position dominates (different streams or the same Event), and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. A position Event whose committed coordinate this Station does not hold is refused with temporarily_unavailable and zero writes; the position need not belong to the read_scope container. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.

Authenticated member's Account Station binds caller_actor_id to the exact session Actor, checks current and target-cut scope/membership/history/policy, and forwards the same selectors to governance over the existing peer material read. Governance independently checks the named Actor's current and target-cut authority and the caller Station's replication right at the target accepted Commit cut; response contains only digest-verified Genesis GroupInfo and ratchet-tree public bytes, never a leaf index, private tree or secret. Unknown and unauthorized selectors are indistinguishable.

Authenticated own Account Station binds the exact session Actor, request selectors and current/target authorization, verifies governance authority and the complete frozen method-native attestor closures and both original historical signatures, then returns the unchanged governance roster page plus purpose-bound public keys. Ordinary clients independently verify manifest, recipient double signatures, ordered digest and RFC leaf/Proposal bindings without a method-history verifier or live resolver. This self-only result is non-portable, has no verified boolean and grants no reusable authorization or current route. Both peer page and exact self projection including key material fit the 2 MiB canonical response limit; governance computes the longest continuous 1..8-record prefix fitting both.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.

ACL-filtered paginated enumeration of the authority streams of one Realm that the caller is permitted to know exist and whose Commit chain is established. It is core, not an extension read: positional scan requires a stream_ref the caller already holds and the subscribe window is bounded to 64 streams, so without enumeration a stream outside the first screen would be undiscoverable and could starve. Pagination is one fixed server-side generation with a per-page permission recheck; a stream that appears later is discovered by a later enumeration or by the visible discovery delta, never inserted into an earlier page. Containers with no Commit yet are omitted rather than reported with an empty head.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Prepares one join, knock or invite acceptance against the Realm's current governance Station. The Station is discovered from the current authority bundle, not from the inviter or genesis Station. Preparation freezes the exact request and current policy revision; final admission is an authority commit and performs no actor-checkpoint, RealmCommit-basis or authority-commit calculation.

Own-Station validated pre-join Realm preview. The caller's own Station takes target.authority_locator_hints (copied from an ak.account.invite_delivery entry or a Directory discovery projection), fetches the RealmAuthorityBundle with its own nonce through ak.open.realm_authority.read.bundle.v1, verifies Realm genesis, the continuous handoff chain and the unexpired nonce-bound current_assertion, and then reads the preview only from that verified current governance Station through ak.peer.realm_join.read.preview.v1, taking the equivalent local path when it is that Station. The inviter Station and Directory are locator hints and never a preview source. The outcome returns the bundle this Station verified and the disclosed public_preview; the client never calls the source or selects a candidate, and the preview is not membership, a join commitment or verified governance state. An unreachable governance Station is a retryable upstream failure and MUST NOT be replaced by another service identity or member Station.
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

Required query realm_id. Returns the exact previously issued closed signed snapshot identified by snapshot_id only to the same authenticated account while Realm and every disclosed row/head/floor remain authorized. A referenced non-preview window requires durable exact retrieval for its consumption lifetime; unavailable references require per-stream preview_only. Response IDs MUST exactly match request IDs; never regenerate, resign or substitute current head.

Continues only the canonical next transaction step. Recovery's terminal step carries the replacement-device-signed recovery receipt; the current governance Station atomically validates both prepared producer Events, issues their two consecutive PCR-stream RealmCommits, advances device generation, activates the device and consumes the session. The client never supplies or signs either RealmCommit.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. SecurityRotation create requires fresh high-risk action authentication judged by the Account Authority and binds authorizing_device_id to the authenticated session; it issues no AuthorizationLease. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.
Transient encrypted Signal rail. It creates no durable Event or RealmCommit, does not advance any authority stream, and grants no delivery or authorization proof.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.

Own Station validates 1..64 exact account-device/Agent current or historical selectors. Current keys serve this validation invocation only. Each historical selector requires committed_event_ref copied from one verified account-subscribe or per-stream-scan stream_row, or from this invocation frozen complete signed self request Event paired with its bound accepted outcome original Commit under server-trusted-results section 2.1; its stream Realm must equal request.realm_id. A bare EventId, current projection, cursor, timestamp, arrival order or cached sighting cannot supply the coordinate, and missing or redacted history remains unavailable without current-query fallback. Current ordinary human account_device returns only public_key_b64u after own-Station verification of the existing exact-device directory at this invocation; no PCR coordinates or history disclosure. Current Agent and every historical resolved key independently carry its accepted authorization_ref as another committed_event_ref plus the verified current revision and governance generation of that authorization stream; the target and authorization refs may differ and must never be forced equal. Exactly one resolved/unavailable result maps by complete selector equality rather than array position; unavailable echoes that complete selector. Request <=64 KiB; each result <=16 KiB; complete response <=1 MiB. Self-submitted Human PCR history requires original same-Station self-admission, authenticated recipient fullAccount equal to actual Human producer fullAccount, exact target and complete immutable original historical authorization/proof. direct_conversation_admission_mappings.transaction_rule: Every mapped rejection is decided before RealmCommit signing and atomically performs zero writes: no Event, RealmCommit, projection, outbox row, dedup success, or other durable effect.
direct_conversation_admission_mappings.retry_rule: A rejected request is not a committed exact replay. A later request is fully reevaluated against the then-current authoritative state and cannot reuse a cached denial or success.

rules.predicate: Any issuer, pair_key, authorization_basis, Realm role, exact-two participant set, main Strand, founding_unit_digest, or initial MLS reference differs from the accepted founding facts or unique scope-derived group state.
The target is the canonical Direct Conversation Realm and the submitted Event requests an irreversible destroy or tombstone.

A new write targets an established Direct Conversation whose immutable binding or authoritative membership projection does not resolve to exactly two distinct principal participants. The membership participant set is the distinct principals of every member typed current row of the Realm, join or leave, so a participant who left still counts and that participant's own ak.member.rejoin.own passes this gate for the participant evaluator; any principal outside the pair fails it.

read_projection.rule: This read-only branch emits no write rejection and performs no durable write.

rules.predicate: An invite or join candidate ActorId is not one of the immutable binding's two exact ActorIds. This rule wins over direct_conversation_invite_forbidden when both predicates match.
An invite flow targets an active Direct Conversation and its candidate, when one is resolvable, is inside the immutable pair. The atomic founding peer join is not an invite and is outside this stage.

A root-reliant Event (root_reliance) requests an action outside the closed mask of the Realm's current phase (masked_actions): the founding phase admits only the exact four-Event founding unit, the materialization phase only the scope's unique ak.mls.genesis and the ak.mls.commit that Adds the other participant with its Welcome, and found admits none. Operational, grant, member-governance, policy and terminal families therefore always fail.

rules.predicate: An allowlisted participant action fails any required binding, exact participant, membership, Realm/Strand/MLS, Contact, device, Agent, resource, or lifecycle check after structural profile guards. All such failures collapse to this non-enumerating reason.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Ordinary authoring and object changes follow registered data execution with verified cached authority. Risk tier does not impose RealmCommit age, online origin or periodic freshness on ordinary publication.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Registered high-risk approvals and explicit validity constraints are enforced. Security writes revalidate exact authority and preconditions in the unique confirmation sequence; risk labels do not override execution classification.

eligibility_kind_definitions.event_submission_carrier: The action executes through a durable Event. An approval requirement is expressible because the registered Event submission operation carries approval evidence beside the complete Event.
eligibility_kind_definitions.registered_operation_carrier: The non-Event action names an explicit operation carrier override whose canonical closed request schema contains the registered evidence field.
eligibility_kind_definitions.ineligible_no_registered_carrier: The action has no registered evidence carrier. A grant approval constraint and an ak.policy.action approval requirement targeting this action are forbidden in v1.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant, except for a root_control_only or subject_only action, whose authority is the registered root-control or subject binding, and except for the subject-bound branches the owning section registers for that event kind (the invitee decline and the joined inviter self-cancel of ak.invite.cancel, zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root typed current result may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

approval_requirement_eligibility is the only v1 decision source for whether a grant approval constraint or ak.policy.action approval requirement may target an action. Every event_mapping_kind resolves through event_mapping_defaults; a non_event_surface action is ineligible unless one exact action_overrides row selects registered_operation_carrier and names a reachable carrier. Implementations MUST NOT infer eligibility from action spelling, risk tier, prose, or an invented action-to-operation mapping.

actions.notes: Authorizes a service-actor signed bridge error Event only for the exact active Applet installation, registration epoch and granted scope. The Event still carries applet_id and a real authorization_ref; service signature is provenance, not authority.

The conditional Event admission and operation validator require the exact active registration/grant/scope and atomic set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.

Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.member_id == envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.member_id != envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId.

Subject-only self-service acceptance. The only authority is that the actor is the invitee of the target Invite (the stored invite_directed_invitee for a directed Invite, the claimed subject for a third-party Invite); an invitee is usually not yet a member and holds no grant, so admission never evaluates a capability and the action is excluded from every derived authority set (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

Grants only the third-party cancellation branch of ak.invite.cancel (target_state=revoked by an actor that is not the inviter). The invitee declining (target_state=rejected) and the still-joined inviter cancelling its own Invite are authorized by the Invite's accepted binding alone and never evaluate this grant (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects realm_alias). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Terminal Realm lifecycle; v1 production admission MUST reject with failed_precondition and zero writes because the independent destructive-confirmation carrier is undefined. It MUST NOT be granted to anyone.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.

registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=inactive, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

Ordinary clients consume bound public keys from their authenticated own Station. This action authorizes no live discovery or current route.

registry_rules: Only an active adapter row can validate a did or project it to did_core_id. DID syntax alone never admits a method.
project is a method-defined semantic transform over a canonical bare did, not generic string concatenation or prefix removal. Receivers compare the complete projected did_core_id byte-for-byte.

Every adapter validates method-native control, deactivation, currentness and history evidence according to its trust profile before returning a verified projection. Unknown methods and unknown adapter versions fail closed.

A new did is an update of an existing principal or service only when the same active adapter projects it to the identical did_core_id. A method or core change creates a new identity and cannot inherit authorization through a continuity assertion.
DID URLs are constructed and compared from the verified did under the adapter's DID URL rules. A did_core_id is never used as a DID URL base.

No adapter exposes expand or core_to_did. Even when a method-specific suffix appears reversible, an isolated did_core_id cannot create resolution authority; the required did or did_url arrives through did-evidence-boundary-registry.json.

A did is a canonical bare DID and therefore contains no path, query or fragment. Each active adapter deterministically emits method_history_head, version_id and service_resolution_event_ref according to its registered rules, including synthetic values for methods without native history.

For a generic Event proof, the verifier extracts the canonical bare did base from proof.verification_method, validates the active adapter and key at the cited accepted-at method history, projects that did, and compares the resulting did_core_id to executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery are the only registered special admissions and never convert current DID control into generic human PCR authority.

A principal resolution update is admitted only in its derived identity-control Realm and only when one exact expected_revision precondition guards ak:result:identity_resolution:null. The guarded whole resolution_projection MUST equal the accepted current typed current result; predecessor event/history coordinates come only from that signed precondition, never from payload mirrors.

Exactly one active adapter, did:webvh:1.0, carries human_principal_anchor=true and declares registration_anchor_kind=webvh_registration; that value is the sole discriminator of the closed principal-registration-anchor contract. A human principal is registered and given PCR genesis only through that branch. Every other method, including did:key and did:web, carries human_principal_anchor=false and MUST fail closed with unsupported_did_method at schema and role admission, before any method parser, history replay or registry write. Adding another human anchor requires a newly registered portable publication-proof or independent-witness trust model with its own threat model and conformance vectors; it MUST NOT enter through a test fixture, an optional sidecar member or a locally widened allowlist.

Direct principal-control proofs have exactly two existing purposes: approval_signature at its signed approved_at and invite_subject_proof at the covering claim RealmCommit committed_at. For a did:webvh principal, a verifier independently authenticates the subject DID SCID and complete native history at that instant, then accepts only a document-declared method or the exact standard did:key:<multibase>#<multibase> of an effective updateKeys member at that instant. The key DID is never projected as the principal identity. No caller key, synthetic root fragment, PCR device key, future state or current-head fallback proves this historical relation. This exception grants no generic Event or SessionGrant authority.

The managed identity_resolution_update producer admitted only by applet-integration.md section 7.3.2.1 is verified against its exact installed managed PCR current native old updateKeys and standard previous-resolution CAS. Its key DID is not the managed Account identity; the original Applet Service authenticates transport only. This admission applies to no human PCR, other managed Actor, generic Event or SessionGrant.
